title: Momentum-Selective Electron and Spin Dynamics under Ultrafast Photoexcitation
authors: Gusein Bedirkhanov, Nagamalleswararao Dasari, Alexander I. Lichtenstein, Evgeny A. Stepanov
abstract: Recent advances in time-resolved spectroscopies have enabled direct access to the momentum-selective nonequilibrium dynamics of correlated quantum materials, revealing a strongly momentum-dependent response of electrons and collective excitations. Interpreting these observations requires a real-time theoretical framework that consistently captures the interplay between strong local electronic correlations and nonlocal collective fluctuations, a capability that remains beyond state-of-the-art nonequilibrium approaches. Using a recently developed real-time many-body framework, we resolve the momentum-selective ultrafast dynamics of a photoexcited correlated electron system. We predict a transient nodal-antinodal anisotropy in electronic heating, providing a microscopic explanation for the momentum-dependent response debated in time-resolved photoemission and Raman experiments, and identify the nonthermal spectral-weight transfer responsible for the transient antinodal in-gap states observed in ultrafast photoemission. We further uncover a momentum-selective magnetic response, in which antiferromagnetic fluctuations undergo a strongly nonthermal, quench-like excitation far above the electronic temperature while preserving their correlation length, before relaxing through a momentum-space magnon cascade toward lower-momentum modes. Finally, by tracking the real-time local spin susceptibility, we identify a dynamical, experimentally accessible signature of local-moment formation and its photoinduced melting. Our results establish a unified microscopic picture of ultrafast electronic and magnetic dynamics, providing a framework for interpreting momentum-resolved pump-probe experiments.
summary: This paper develops a sophisticated real-time many-body theory to model how electrons and spins behave immediately after being excited by intense light in correlated materials. It successfully predicts momentum-dependent electronic heating anisotropies and details the complex, nonthermal dynamics of magnetic fluctuations. The work establishes a unified picture for interpreting advanced pump-probe experiments across both charge and spin sectors.
main_problem: To develop a unified microscopic theoretical framework for understanding momentum-selective ultrafast electronic and magnetic dynamics in correlated quantum materials following photoexcitation.
main_result: The study predicts transient nodal–antinodal anisotropy in electronic heating, explains the origin of in-gap states via nonthermal spectral-weight transfer, and characterizes the quench-like excitation of antiferromagnetic fluctuations.
method: The authors employ a real-time many-body framework, specifically the real-time dual GW (D-GW) method, to track non-equilibrium dynamics.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Hubbard model on a square lattice, describing correlated electron systems. The analysis extends to studying local spin and charge susceptibilities in dimer models as well.
key_observables: Momentum-selective electronic response (Nodal vs. Antinodal), electronic heating anisotropy, nonthermal spectral-weight transfer, AFM mode dynamics, and real-time local spin susceptibility.
important_parameters: $U$ (local repulsion) varied in $[0.5, 1.5]$, ultrafast photoexcitation pulse parameters, and temperature ($T=0$ vs $T>0$).
main_assumptions: The D-GW method is used to consistently capture the interplay between strong local correlations and nonlocal collective fluctuations in real time.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time-domain electric field and momentum-resolved spectral functions, showing the nodal–antinodal dichotomy in equilibrium and tracking dynamic changes upon photoexcitation.
paper_structure: The work establishes the need for a unified theory, applies D-GW to analyze electronic response (N vs AN), extends this analysis to collective magnetic excitations ($	ext{AFM}$ fluctuations), and concludes by linking these findings to local moment formation via spin susceptibility.
why_interesting: This research provides advanced theoretical tools (D-GW) for simulating non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, which is highly relevant for understanding ultrafast response in strongly correlated materials that are often studied using pump-probe spectroscopy techniques.
